a.title: The answer

a.text: The answer: A hardware timer, started at boot (a privileged act),

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: interrupts every few milliseconds and lands in the kernel like a

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: trap. Solved: while(1); with no system call; two lines in

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: usertrap turn the tick into a switch. Cost: a tick's worth of

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: kernel work, many times a second.

a.title: The answer

a.text: The answer: A context switch stores 14 kernel registers into A's

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: record and loads B's; loading the stack pointer is the switch;

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: the user registers were already in the trapframe. Solved: the CPU

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: still held A's registers after the kernel chose B. Cost: about 1

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: µs a switch, plus a cold cache.
